artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: The comparison producer, beside the holdings producer and reading its declaration. ONE ROW PER BRONZE FILE, no file dropped and no figure invented. Composition (ruling 7) is a column slice and two row sums over a date-by-account matrix of account_value * daily_return and account_value: a level's accounts are unioned and weighted by account_value, which already IS the prior-day basket, so the composite is value-weighted rather than averaged. The chain window is HALF-OPEN -- a gold row dated `start` is the move INTO start, and including it would add a day the vendor's figure does not carry. A day with no computable row for a mapped account is counted in `partial_days` and flagged on the row, never treated as a flat day. Run ad hoc for QA; no schedule, no alarm, no standing comparator (CLAUDE.md's moratorium and ruling 12). Naming gate on the new file: PASS, 0 graded. commit-gate clean.

The 49F entry grows a `comparison` block: the bronze and cross-reference prefixes as TEMPLATES (the literal paths carry the firm's registered short token, which the naming limb refuses in an authored file), the vendor return path, the stated bases, and the period rule with its measured denominators. NEITHER JOIN COLUMN IS NAMED: see the xref artifact below.

python -m pytest data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_holdings_performance/tests/ -q -> 39 passed (24 from er-301, 15 new). The order's step 4 asks for the composition, the period selection and EACH named reason, and each is a hand-derivable fixture: a two-account level where 9,000 at +10% beside 1,000 at -10% must read +0.08 and not the 0.00 an average gives; two +10% days chaining to +0.21 and not +0.20, with the half-open window separating +0.21 from +0.331; a missing day counted as partial rather than flat; the longest-fully-covered rule with its dedup of the repeated range, its earliest-start tie-break (asserted on the list AND its reverse, because a rule that depends on list order is not a rule), and a null vendor return never becoming a candidate; one test per reason; and a schema test asserting the row dict, the column list and the arrow schema are one contract.

artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: TWO partitions, one per as-of date the bronze filenames carry. Read back independently of the producer: date=2026-06-30 footer 1 row, date=2026-08-28 footer 5,317 rows, 5,318 total against 5,318 bronze files, 5,318 distinct source_key, 0 duplicated, 24 columns. 5,278 rows carry both figures and a period; 40 carry a named reason (PERIOD-OUTSIDE-GOLD 35, NO-VENDOR-FIGURE 4, ACCOUNT-UNRESOLVED 1); 0 rows carry neither. Each partition also carries a manifest.json with the reason census, both bases and the selection rule. Nothing reads this table. || WHAT THE COMPARISON MEASURED, three findings, all `measured`. [FWD13-F1] WHERE BOTH METHODS HAVE SOMETHING TO MEASURE, THEY AGREE. Of the 4,256 fully-covered comparison rows (no partial days), 4,098 are on accounts that still held priced positions at the period end, and 3,994 of those 4,098 -- 97.5% -- agree within 5 percentage points over a 251-trading-day year, with a median absolute difference of 1.64pp. The sign is consistent and expected: the median difference is -1.62pp, Opal below the vendor, which is the shape of a basis that carries no income and no flow term against one that does. [FWD13-F2] THE TAIL IS NEAR-EMPTY ACCOUNTS, NOT A PRODUCER DEFECT, AND A CONSUMER MUST NOT READ IT AS ONE. 20 fully-covered rows differ by more than 50 percentage points; 16 of them are accounts whose gold row holds ZERO priced positions at the period end (account_value median $112.00, minimum $1.09), where the holdings basis correctly reads 0.00% per day because the account is cash, while the vendor's time-weighted figure on the same account ranges -74.1% to +150.0% because it is driven by flows into and out of a near-empty book. Three worked examples at date=2026-08-28: accounts ending 1531, 2884 and 1173 carry account_value 334.67, 52.39 and 317.48 with included_count 0, against vendor returns of +150.0%, +144.6% and +146.6%. This is the two bases being structurally incomparable on a shell account, which is what FWD-13 exists to make visible -- but the comparison table does not carry account_value, so a reader cannot see it from the row alone. [FWD13-F3] 1,022 of 5,278 compared rows (19.4%) are PARTIAL -- at least one trading day in the selected period has no computable gold row for the mapped account -- and their differences are not usable as a comparison: the median is -0.99pp but the maximum absolute difference is 13.98, against 1.50 among fully-covered rows. `opal_partial` and `partial_days` are on every row precisely so a reader can exclude them; a consumer that ignores those two columns will read a partial chain as a full-period return.

THE ACCOUNT MAP, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE ORDER NAMED -- declared under declared_exclusions with the measurement that forced it. Read only; this cell writes nothing here. 6,202 rows, 6,202 distinct vendor ids, 5,376 resolved, 826 unresolved. BOTH JOIN COLUMNS ARE FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, NOT TYPED: resolve_xref_columns() takes the vendor-side column to be the one whose values actually contain the ids read from a 32-file bronze probe, and the custodian-side column to be the one whose values match the entry's declared account_id_zero_pad form, REFUSING if either test matches anything other than exactly one column. Two reasons, and the second is the better one: the column names carry another pipeline's vendor token which the naming limb refuses here, AND typing a join key assumes it while measuring it checks it -- an ambiguous join key does not fail, it produces a plausible wrong answer. The resolved pair is printed on every run ('join bd_account_id -> schwab_account_id (matched, not typed)').

declared_exclusions.item: Mapping the vendor account to the gold by its `accountNumber`, as the order's step 2 words it
declared_exclusions.reason: IT CANNOT BE DONE AS WRITTEN, and the criterion was not weakened to make it look as though it could. The bronze `accountNumber` is MASKED to its last four characters ('XXXX5115') in 40 of 40 sampled files, and last-four does not identify an account: the 7,540 gold account ids hold only 5,279 distinct last-four values, 1,801 of those values are shared by more than one account, 4,062 accounts sit in an ambiguous bucket, and 23 of 40 sampled vendor accounts land in one. The landed account cross-reference carries the map instead, keyed on the same `externalId` the bronze already publishes, and an unresolved row becomes the NAMED reason ACCOUNT-UNRESOLVED rather than a guess. The order's intent -- map the vendor account to the gold's account id -- is met; its named mechanism is not, and that substitution is this entry.

declared_exclusions.item: Comparing against the vendor's money-weighted return, its benchmarks, or any period the gold does not wholly cover
declared_exclusions.reason: Ruling 8 names the vendor's official TIME-weighted figure as the comparison point. `moneyWeightedReturns` and the per-benchmark returns are present in the same node and are deliberately not read. A period the gold does not wholly cover is refused rather than truncated, because a full vendor figure against a partial Opal one is the silent failure FWD-13 exists to prevent; 35 files carry PERIOD-OUTSIDE-GOLD for exactly this reason (the 49F gold begins 2024-07-09 and their only ranges are calendar 2024 or earlier).
